rationale: Codex's plan is the strongest base because the things it gets right are the architecturally expensive ones to retrofit — parent-directory grants reasoned correctly against a harness that launches once per pane, one shell template instead of a second that would re-open the drift the launcher library exists to prevent, one justified module with no new test files, and coverage of doctor, wipe-time removeWorktree, and uninstall — whereas the repository-scope guard my own plan uniquely gets right (without it I measured 14 fast-suite failures, since blocking bare `status`/`diff` also blocks the `pnpm check:fast` every plan requires before committing) is a few portable lines any wrapper can adopt; its remaining fixes are to resolve the target repository rather than delegating on every `-C`/`--git-dir` selector, to name the input its `git show` condition reads, and to drop the 0o500 directory mode, which I verified makes wipeIssue's rmSync fail with ENOTEMPTY and abort the wipe with the whole issue runtime intact.
